subject.title: feat: let agents remember across private conversations

question: Should OpenClaw ship the default-off `rememberAcrossConversations` mode as the supported owner-controlled authorization boundary for same-agent private transcript recall?
rationale: The patch adds both a durable configuration surface and a sensitive cross-conversation data-access contract; correctness tests cannot decide whether that product boundary is the intended long-term policy.

options.title: Accept the bounded mode after repair
options.body: Keep the default-off per-agent setting and land it after the doctor null-safety repair, with the documented same-agent/private-only boundary as the supported contract.

options.title: Defer product direction
options.body: Pause the feature and retain existing advanced memory configuration until maintainers choose a broader identity or transcript-sharing model.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded mode after repair
recommendation.body: Keep the default-off per-agent setting and land it after the doctor null-safety repair, with the documented same-agent/private-only boundary as the supported contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Steipete carried the current rebase and repair sequence and is best positioned to route the outstanding product-boundary decision.
